USWDS RenderbyOddball

Ask in plain words. Get a User Interface you can use.

A text chatbot hands back a paragraph and wishes you luck. USWDS Render answers with a UI using the components your site already ships, and lets users take straightforward actions.

The Landscape

Your website is designed, tested, and accessible. Everyone gets the same page, every time.

It also answers only with what somebody planned for, one screen at a time. People rarely arrive with the question the menu was built for.

A text chatbot will answer anything. In paragraphs.

Nothing to interact with, and a different shape every time. Text chatbots can, at best, awkwardly guide a user to an existing page.

The Oddball Solution

USWDS Render answers in the components your site already ships. They are the same parts, but arranged for the question that was actually asked.

See It In Action

Someone types their question in the words they would use on the phone.

37 seconds later the answer is a page. Two plans priced against those drugs, and a button under each.

One click and you're enrolled in the plan.

13 seconds later the request is in. A confirmation number, and where it sits in the process.

Follow up with details. No dead ends. Another button for more information.

Faster Outcomes

One errand: a Part D plan that covers Eliquis and Jardiance. Three ways to run it.

By phone. A menu tree, a hold, then describing both drugs to a person and writing down the plans they read back to you.

On the website. Find the plan finder, enter the ZIP, add each drug and each dosage, set the filters, compare the results, then start the enrollment.

Here. Ask in the words you would have used on the phone. Read two plans. Click one. Fifty seconds of waiting, question to confirmation number.

What You Control

Reliability comes from what the model never touches.

The catalog. Forty nine USWDS components, and whatever else your organization wants to include. The model picks from that list, and nothing outside it renders.

The components. Accessibility lives in the component, not in whatever got generated this time. Fix it once and every render after that follows the change.

The data. Every figure on that page came back from a tool you own and can audit.

The actions. Buttons pull from a list of predefined actions. Users interact with their information predictably.

How It Works

There are three parts to every answer.

Tools fetch the facts. That answer took five tool calls: ZIP to county, drug lookup, plan search, and two cost estimates. Clicking Choose was a sixth. Nothing on the page came out of the model's memory.

The model writes a spec, not a page. It picks a component you registered, fills in its props, and binds the button to a predefined action. This is that spec, read straight out of the app.

Your components render it. Every name maps to code your site already ships, so the accessibility work is done and already tested. The button does the one thing you allowed and nothing else.

A chatbot's range. Your website's guarantees.
